title: ISO 513 workpiece material groups, and how a material named in Specify is placed in one

source.agreement: both give the six groups and what each holds (read 2026-11-07)

groups.P: steel and cast steel, other than stainless steel (ISO 513 puts some ferritic and martensitic stainless in P; this table places every stainless steel in M, as tool makers commonly do)
groups.N: non-ferrous metals, such as aluminium and copper alloys, and non-metallic materials
groups.H: hardened steel and chilled cast iron

placing._comment: A stand-in until specify-core gives the material's family (step2cam docs/upstream-needs.md, S2): specify-core's answer is the material's name (part.material), so its words are matched. The name is split into lower-case words; an entry matches when one of its words, or phrases of words, appears whole. A name with a word in `never` (a printing process, or no material) gets no group; otherwise the first entry that matches places it. Tool steel goes in P, as supplied; hardened it is H, which the name does not say. A name nothing matches gets no group, and the tools' own cutting data are used. Alloy 6082 (including 6082-T6) is explicitly aluminium from Hydro’s EN AW-6082 datasheet; other unqualified alloy numbers remain unknown.
